Memophant 2.1.0

The autonomy release: your project memory now largely maintains itself, and everything the app tells you about that work is honest.

New

  • Memory Review window. Review is a dedicated, resizable window per project. Every item shows the evidence you need: real before/after diffs, conflicts side-by-side, masked context for secret blocks, and staleness banners. Actions stay pinned in view.
  • Charter drafting with Claude. Claude can draft a project charter — manually or in the background — into a review pen. You remain the only one who can save the charter; every write is secret-scanned.
  • Autonomous Steward for everyone. Background curation and trusted auto-apply are now on by default, including existing installs (Settings opt-out). Every applied change is one click to revert.

Improved

  • Counts you can trust. The "Review N" button, health card, and review window count the same things — a button's number is exactly the rows you'll see. Give-ups are reviewable and clearable.
  • Honest progress. Drain progress shows what the run will actually do; spot-checks and consolidation report their own phases; the quality signal measures challenges against the fixes they challenge.
  • Faster curation. One corpus scan per drain, clustered notes with a single verifier pass, and pre-resolved drift evidence.
  • Activity feed accuracy. Drift rows stop re-announcing on launch and no longer double-count commits across tiers; Steward edits are attributed.

Fixed

  • Reverting an auto-applied fix now correctly reduces the Steward's trust for that kind of change.
  • The review count could read "Review 39" over an empty list; the backlog is now garbage-collected and surfaced.
  • Detached (browse-only) projects can no longer be written to by any drafting or curation path.
  • Hand-edited instruction files with ambiguous markers are reported instead of silently skipped.
  • Numerous copy fixes so no surface claims more than the app actually did.
